corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN (unchanged). Both ingredients are classical: concave minimisation on a line-free polyhedron attains its minimum at a vertex (Hirsch-Hoffman 1961, Thm 3.1/Cor 3.2), and Laguerre's rule bounds the zeros of Dirichlet polynomials (Jameson 2006, Thm 3.1/Cor 3.2). The same finite-vertex pigeonhole appears at the s->infinity end in Fung-Mangasarian 2011 (Prop. 1) and Mangasarian 1999. No source was found stating that the argmin vertex set of sum v^{1/s} is piecewise constant with finitely many switches over all s, or applying this to Gamma_s(p). The paper's proof is correct, and the checker's wording fix is already in cyclic.tex.
issues: (1) ge2011note is misapplied. I read the preprint. Thm 3 ('BFS = local minimisers') is stated for standard form {Ax=b, x>=0} with the objective over ALL variables, and the BFS=>local-min direction uses the entering variable's (eps d)^p term. Adding slacks to P_p gives them zero objective weight, so that direction fails. My recomputed counterexample: P={v>=0: v1+v2>=1, 0.4v1+1.2v2>=1}, vertex (0.25,0.75), feasible direction (-t,+t), and sqrt-sum falls 1.3660 -> 1.3416 at t=0.05. The checker's recommended sentence 'for lp objectives with 0<p<1, the vertices are exactly the local minimisers [ge2011note]' is therefore false for P_p. Drop it; Ge et al. can be cited only for local-min => vertex, or for NP-hardness (Thm 1). (2) hirsch1961extreme: content now verified from the IMM-NYU 277 report (Feb 1961, archive.org), the preprint of the CPAM paper. Thm 3.1 says the infimum of a concave function bounded below is attained iff it is attained on the extreme points of the L-perp section, and then it is attained there. Cor 3.2 says it is attained on any closed convex polyhedron. The theorem numbers come from the report version. The citation survives. (3) jameson2006counting: author PDF read. Thm 3.1 bounds the zeros by the sign changes, and Cor 3.2 by n-1, with the same e^{-p_k x}/Rolle proof as the paper. Survives. (4) Missed prior art, all at the s->infinity endpoint: Fung & Mangasarian JOTA 151(1):1-10, 2011 (Prop. 1, read in full) use the finite-vertex-set argument along q=1/p->infinity for Ax=a, Bx>=b, which includes inequality form like P_p. Mangasarian, Optimization 45:149-162, 1999 (abstract read) shows a vertex solution of minimal support exists and a smooth exponential approximation is exact at a finite parameter. Neither gives a switch count or the whole-range piecewise-constant structure, so novelty of the combination stands. Free corollary: on the last s-interval, the maximiser is a minimum-support vertex of P_p. (5) Search limits: WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200), Semantic Scholar 429, and DuckDuckGo served a bot page after one round. I searched through the Crossref/OpenAlex/arXiv/StackExchange APIs and direct fetches, and found no statement of the full proposition. Rockafellar Cor. 32.3.4 was not read (download failed), so do not cite a corollary number from it unverified.

extra_citations.why: Prop. 1: over a bounded polyhedron {Ax=a, Bx>=b}, the concave ell_p objective has a vertex solution for each q=1/p (via Rockafellar Cor. 32.3.3/32.3.4). Since the vertices are finite, one vertex solves along an infinite sequence of q and is ell_0-minimal. This is the same finite-vertex argument as prop:shapes (i)+(ii), at the s->infinity end only, with no switch count. Full tech report read; metadata confirmed via Crossref.

A concave minimisation over a polyhedron that has a solution has a vertex solution of minimal support. A parametric smooth concave (exponential) approximation solves the minimum-support problem exactly at a finite parameter value, which is the parametric-family finite-vertex pigeonhole. Abstract read from the UW tech report; metadata confirmed via Crossref.
